questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Convert 101101₂ to a base ten number.
questions.explanation: Write the place values from the right: 1×1 + 0×2 + 1×4 + 1×8 + 0×16 + 1×32 = 1 + 4 + 8 + 32 = 45.

whyNot.A: 43 comes from misreading a digit; add the place values carefully.
whyNot.B: 90 is 101101 read as base ten and halved, not a conversion.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.explanation: 0.0024 × 0.5 = 0.0012. Then 0.0012 ÷ 0.03 = 12 ÷ 300 = 0.04 (multiply top and bottom by 10,000 to clear the decimals).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Given that log₁₀2 = 0.3010, find log₁₀8.

whyNot.A: 0.6020 is 2 × log₁₀2, which is log₁₀4.
whyNot.B: 2.4080 is 8 × 0.3010: the power multiplies the log, not the number 8.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: A trader sold an article for ₦2,750 and made a profit of 10%. What was the cost price?
questions.explanation: Selling price = 110% of cost price. Cost price = 2,750 ÷ 1.1 = ₦2,500.

whyNot.D: ₦2,475 takes 10% off the selling price, but the profit is 10% of the cost price.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Solve 3x − 7 = 2x + 5.
questions.explanation: Subtract 2x from both sides: x − 7 = 5. Add 7: x = 12. Check: 3(12) − 7 = 29 and 2(12) + 5 = 29.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the roots of x² − 5x + 6 = 0.
questions.explanation: Factorise: x² − 5x + 6 = (x − 2)(x − 3). So x − 2 = 0 or x − 3 = 0, giving x = 2 or x = 3.

whyNot.C: The signs are wrong: (x + 2)(x + 3) would give x² + 5x + 6.
whyNot.B: 1 and 6 multiply to 6 but add to 7, not 5.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: If f(x) = 2x² − 3x + 1, find f(−2).

whyNot.C: 3 comes from taking (−2)² as −4. A square is never negative.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the sum of the first 10 terms of the arithmetic progression 3, 7, 11, …

whyNot.D: 39 is the 10th term (3 + 9 × 4), not the sum.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: What is the sum of the interior angles of a hexagon?
questions.explanation: Sum of interior angles = (n − 2) × 180°. A hexagon has 6 sides: (6 − 2) × 180° = 720°.

whyNot.A: 540° is for a pentagon (5 sides).
whyNot.B: 360° is the sum of the exterior angles of any polygon.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: If sin θ = 3/5 and θ is acute, find tan θ.
questions.explanation: Draw a right-angled triangle with opposite = 3 and hypotenuse = 5. The adjacent side is √(5² − 3²) = 4. tan θ = opposite/adjacent = 3/4.

whyNot.D: 4/5 is cos θ.
whyNot.A: 4/3 is adjacent/opposite, which is 1/tan θ.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the distance between the points (2, 3) and (5, 7).

whyNot.D: 25 is the square of the distance; take the square root.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: A chord 8 cm long is 3 cm from the centre of a circle. Find the radius of the circle.
questions.explanation: The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord, giving a right-angled triangle with sides 4 cm (half the chord) and 3 cm. Radius = √(4² + 3²) = 5 cm.

whyNot.A: √55 uses the whole chord (8² − 3²); use half the chord.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find dy/dx if y = 3x⁴ − 2x² + 5.
questions.explanation: Differentiate term by term: d/dx(3x⁴) = 12x³, d/dx(−2x²) = −4x, and the constant 5 gives 0. So dy/dx = 12x³ − 4x.

whyNot.D: The derivative of a constant (5) is 0.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Evaluate ∫(4x³ + 2x) dx.
questions.explanation: Raise each power by one and divide by the new power: ∫4x³ dx = x⁴ and ∫2x dx = x². So the answer is x⁴ + x² + c.

whyNot.A: 12x² + 2 is the derivative, not the integral.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the gradient of the curve y = x² − 4x + 1 at the point where x = 3.

whyNot.C: −2 is the value of y at x = 3 (9 − 12 + 1), not the gradient.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the minimum value of y = x² − 6x + 10.
questions.explanation: dy/dx = 2x − 6 = 0 gives x = 3. Then y = 9 − 18 + 10 = 1. (Or complete the square: y = (x − 3)² + 1, which is least when x = 3.)

whyNot.C: 3 is the value of x at the minimum, not the minimum value of y.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the mean of 4, 7, 9, 3 and 7.
questions.explanation: Mean = sum ÷ number of values = (4 + 7 + 9 + 3 + 7) ÷ 5 = 30 ÷ 5 = 6.

whyNot.D: 7 is the mode (the most frequent value).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the median of 12, 5, 8, 15, 10 and 7.
questions.explanation: Arrange in order: 5, 7, 8, 10, 12, 15. With six values, the median is the mean of the 3rd and 4th: (8 + 10) ÷ 2 = 9.

whyNot.D: Don't pick a middle value from the unsorted list: sort first.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: A fair die is thrown once. What is the probability of getting a number greater than 4?
questions.explanation: The numbers greater than 4 are 5 and 6: 2 outcomes out of 6. Probability = 2/6 = 1/3.

whyNot.D: 1/6 is the chance of one particular number.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the range of 23, 17, 31, 9 and 26.
questions.explanation: Range = highest − lowest = 31 − 9 = 22.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Express 0.000357 in standard form.
questions.explanation: Move the decimal point 4 places to the right to get 3.57, a number between 1 and 10. So 0.000357 = 3.57 × 10⁻⁴.

whyNot.D: 35.7 × 10⁻⁵ has the right value, but standard form needs a number from 1 to less than 10 in front.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Simplify 2⅓ + 1¾.

whyNot.B: Fractions can't be added by adding tops and bottoms; use a common denominator (12).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the simple interest on ₦5,000 for 3 years at 4% per annum.

whyNot.A: ₦624.32 is compound interest, not simple interest.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Evaluate 27^(2/3).
questions.explanation: 27^(2/3) = (∛27)² = 3² = 9. Take the cube root first, then square.

whyNot.A: 3 is only the cube root; the power 2 still has to be applied.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Factorise 6x² + x − 2.
questions.explanation: Find two numbers that multiply to 6 × (−2) = −12 and add to 1: 4 and −3. 6x² + 4x − 3x − 2 = 2x(3x + 2) − 1(3x + 2) = (2x − 1)(3x + 2).

whyNot.A: (2x + 1)(3x − 2) = 6x² − x − 2: the middle sign is wrong.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Solve the simultaneous equations x + y = 7 and x − y = 1.
questions.explanation: Add the equations: 2x = 8, so x = 4. Then 4 + y = 7, so y = 3. Check: 4 − 3 = 1.

whyNot.D: x = 3, y = 4 gives x − y = −1, not 1.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Make r the subject of the formula V = πr²h.
questions.explanation: Divide both sides by πh: r² = V ÷ πh. Take the square root: r = √(V ÷ πh).

whyNot.A: V ÷ πh is r², not r.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Solve the inequality 2x − 3 > 7.
questions.explanation: Add 3 to both sides: 2x > 10. Divide by 2: x > 5. (The sign only flips when you multiply or divide by a negative number.)

whyNot.B: We divided by a positive number, so the sign stays the same.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the area of a circle of radius 7 cm. (Take π = 22/7.)

whyNot.C: 44 cm is the circumference (2πr), not the area.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the volume of a cuboid measuring 5 cm by 4 cm by 3 cm.
questions.explanation: Volume = length × breadth × height = 5 × 4 × 3 = 60 cm³.

whyNot.A: 94 cm² is the total surface area, not the volume.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the curved surface area of a cylinder of radius 3.5 cm and height 10 cm. (Take π = 22/7.)
questions.explanation: Curved surface area = 2πrh = 2 × 22/7 × 3.5 × 10 = 220 cm².

whyNot.D: 110 cm² is πrh: the 2 is missing.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the perimeter of a sector of a circle of radius 7 cm with an angle of 90° at the centre. (Take π = 22/7.)
questions.explanation: Arc length = 90/360 × 2 × 22/7 × 7 = 11 cm. The perimeter adds the two radii: 11 + 7 + 7 = 25 cm.

whyNot.A: 11 cm is the arc alone; the two radii are part of the perimeter.
whyNot.D: 38.5 cm² is the area of the sector.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Each exterior angle of a regular polygon is 40°. How many sides has the polygon?
questions.explanation: The exterior angles of any polygon add up to 360°. Number of sides = 360° ÷ 40° = 9.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: The two shorter sides of a right-angled triangle are 6 cm and 8 cm. Find the hypotenuse.
questions.explanation: By Pythagoras: hypotenuse² = 6² + 8² = 36 + 64 = 100. Hypotenuse = 10 cm.

whyNot.A: 14 cm just adds the sides; square them first.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: What is the value of cos 60°?
questions.explanation: In an equilateral triangle of side 2 cut in half, the side next to the 60° angle is 1 and the hypotenuse is 2. cos 60° = 1/2.

whyNot.D: √3/2 is sin 60° (or cos 30°).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: What is the angle at the circumference subtended by a diameter of a circle?
questions.explanation: The angle in a semicircle is a right angle: the angle at the centre is 180°, and the angle at the circumference is half of it, 90°.

whyNot.A: 180° is the angle at the centre (a straight line).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the mode of 2, 3, 3, 5, 7, 3, 5.
questions.explanation: The mode is the value that appears most often. 3 appears three times, more than any other value.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: A bag contains 4 red balls and 6 blue balls. A ball is picked at random. What is the probability that it is red?
questions.explanation: There are 4 + 6 = 10 balls and 4 are red. Probability = 4/10 = 2/5.

whyNot.A: 2/3 is red compared with blue (4 : 6); probability compares red with all the balls.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: In a pie chart of 60 students, what angle represents 15 students?

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: The mean of x, x + 2 and x + 4 is 10. Find x.

whyNot.D: 10 is the mean, which here is the middle value x + 2.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Convert 234 (base five) to a base ten number.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Write 0.0045672 correct to 3 significant figures.
questions.explanation: The first significant figure is the 4. Keep three: 4, 5, 6, then look at the next digit (7). It is 5 or more, so round up: 0.00457.

whyNot.A: 0.00456 drops the 7 instead of rounding up.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: A man spends 2/5 of his salary on rent and 1/3 on food. What fraction of his salary is left?

whyNot.C: 11/15 is what he spends, not what is left.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Share ₦600 in the ratio 2 : 3. What is the larger share?
questions.explanation: Total parts = 2 + 3 = 5. One part = 600 ÷ 5 = ₦120. Larger share = 3 × 120 = ₦360.

whyNot.A: ₦240 is the smaller share.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Expand (2x + 3)².

whyNot.D: Squaring a sum gives a middle term too: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b².
whyNot.A: The middle term is 2 × 2x × 3 = 12x.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.explanation: 16 = 2⁴, so 2^(x + 1) = 2⁴. Equate the powers: x + 1 = 4, so x = 3.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the sum of the roots of 2x² − 7x + 3 = 0.
questions.explanation: For ax² + bx + c = 0, the sum of the roots is −b/a = 7/2. (The roots are 3 and 1/2, which add to 7/2.)

whyNot.C: 3/2 is the product of the roots (c/a).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: y varies directly as x, and y = 12 when x = 4. Find y when x = 7.
questions.explanation: y = kx. 12 = 4k gives k = 3. When x = 7, y = 3 × 7 = 21.

whyNot.C: 3 is the constant k, not y.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the area of a triangle with base 10 cm and height 6 cm.
questions.explanation: Area = ½ × base × height = ½ × 10 × 6 = 30 cm².

whyNot.D: 60 cm² leaves out the ½.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the volume of a cone of radius 3 cm and height 7 cm. (Take π = 22/7.)
questions.explanation: Volume = ⅓πr²h = ⅓ × 22/7 × 9 × 7 = ⅓ × 198 = 66 cm³.

whyNot.B: 198 cm³ is the volume of a cylinder with the same radius and height; a cone is a third of it.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the total surface area of a cube of edge 4 cm.
questions.explanation: A cube has 6 square faces, each 4 × 4 = 16 cm². Total = 6 × 16 = 96 cm².

whyNot.A: 64 is the volume in cm³.
whyNot.D: 16 cm² is one face.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the area of a trapezium whose parallel sides are 8 cm and 12 cm and whose height is 5 cm.
questions.explanation: Area = ½ × (sum of parallel sides) × height = ½ × (8 + 12) × 5 = 50 cm².

whyNot.D: 100 cm² leaves out the ½.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Two angles of a triangle are 47° and 68°. Find the third angle.
questions.explanation: Angles in a triangle add up to 180°. Third angle = 180° − 47° − 68° = 65°.

whyNot.B: 115° is the sum of the two angles given.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Town B is due east of town A. What is the bearing of B from A?
questions.explanation: Bearings are measured clockwise from north, in three figures. East is a quarter turn clockwise from north: 090°.

whyNot.D: 270° is due west.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: If tan x = 1 and 0° < x < 90°, find x.
questions.explanation: tan x = 1 means the opposite and adjacent sides are equal, as in a right-angled isosceles triangle, so x = 45°.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the gradient of the line joining (1, 2) and (3, 8).
questions.explanation: Gradient = (change in y) ÷ (change in x) = (8 − 2) ÷ (3 − 1) = 6 ÷ 2 = 3.

whyNot.D: 1/3 divides the change in x by the change in y: it's the other way round.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the median of 3, 9, 4, 7 and 5.
questions.explanation: In order: 3, 4, 5, 7, 9. The middle (3rd) value is 5.

whyNot.A: 5.6 is the mean.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Two fair coins are tossed together. What is the probability of getting two heads?
questions.explanation: The outcomes are HH, HT, TH and TT, all equally likely. Only HH is two heads: 1 out of 4.

whyNot.D: 1/3 treats 'one head and one tail' as a single outcome, but HT and TH are different.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: The scores 1, 2 and 3 have frequencies 2, 5 and 3. Find the mean score.

whyNot.A: 2 is the mode (it has the highest frequency).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: A number is chosen at random from 1 to 20. What is the probability that it is a multiple of 5?
questions.explanation: The multiples of 5 are 5, 10, 15 and 20: 4 out of 20. Probability = 4/20 = 1/5.

questions.subject: use-of-english
questions.context: When the rains failed for a second year, the farmers of Ogbede did not wait for help from the city. They dug shallow wells along the dry riverbed, shared the water by turns, and planted beans, which need less water than yams. The elders, who had at first doubted the plan, were soon its loudest supporters. By harvest time the village had food to sell as well as to eat. Visitors who came expecting to find hunger found, instead, a market.
questions.stem: Why did the farmers plant beans?
options: Beans sell for more than yams
Beans need less water than yams
questions.explanation: The passage says they planted beans, “which need less water than yams”: in a drought, that was the reason.

whyNot.B: The passage says nothing about prices.
whyNot.A: The elders doubted the plan at first; beans weren't their idea.

questions.explanation: Not waiting for outside help, and solving the problem themselves, shows self-reliance.

questions.explanation: The elders “had at first doubted the plan” but “were soon its loudest supporters”.

questions.stem: The visitors “found, instead, a market”. This implies that the village
options: was visited by traders from the city
had more food than it needed and could sell some
questions.explanation: A market where hunger was expected means the village had a surplus: “food to sell as well as to eat”.

questions.stem: As used in the passage, “shared the water by turns” means that the water was
options: used by each person in a fixed order
questions.explanation: Taking turns means each person uses it one after another, in an agreed order, so everyone gets some.

questions.subject: use-of-english

questions.stem: Which of these is the most suitable title for the passage?
questions.explanation: The whole passage is about how the village coped with failed rains and ended with food to sell.

whyNot.C: The elders are only part of the story.

questions.subject: use-of-english
questions.stem: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals: The minister gave a CANDID account of the crisis.
questions.explanation: Candid means honest and direct, without hiding anything: frank.

questions.subject: use-of-english
questions.stem: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in capitals: The new manager is very FRUGAL with money.
questions.explanation: Frugal means careful not to waste money. Its opposite is extravagant: spending freely or wastefully.

whyNot.A: Careful is close in meaning to frugal, not opposite.
whyNot.C: Stingy is also close in meaning (if negative).

questions.subject: use-of-english
questions.stem: Neither the teacher nor the students ___ aware of the change.
questions.explanation: With neither … nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject. “Students” is plural, so “were”.

whyNot.B: “Was” would agree with “teacher”, but the verb follows the subject nearer to it.

questions.subject: use-of-english
questions.stem: He has been living in Kano ___ 2019.
questions.explanation: Use “since” with a point in time (2019) and “for” with a length of time (for five years).

questions.subject: use-of-english
questions.stem: After the argument, the brothers decided to BURY THE HATCHET. This means they decided to
questions.explanation: “Bury the hatchet” is an idiom meaning to end a quarrel and become friends again.

questions.subject: use-of-english
questions.stem: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: Accommodation has a double c and a double m: ac-com-mo-da-tion.

questions.subject: use-of-english
questions.stem: The committee ___ submitted its report.
questions.explanation: Here the committee acts as one body (“its report”), so it takes a singular verb: has.

questions.subject: use-of-english
questions.stem: If I ___ you, I would accept the offer.
questions.explanation: For an imagined situation (“if I were you”), standard English uses “were” with every subject.

questions.subject: use-of-english
questions.stem: Which word has a different vowel sound from the others?
questions.explanation: Seat, meet and heat have the long vowel /iː/. Sit has the short vowel /ɪ/.

questions.subject: use-of-english
questions.stem: Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as the one in “food”.
questions.explanation: Food and rude have the long vowel /uː/. Good and foot have the short /ʊ/; flood has /ʌ/.

questions.subject: use-of-english
questions.stem: Which word is stressed on the second syllable?
questions.explanation: pho-TOG-ra-phy is stressed on the second syllable. PHO-to-graph, TA-ble and WA-ter are stressed on the first.

questions.subject: use-of-english
questions.stem: Which word has the same consonant sound as the “ch” in “machine”?
questions.explanation: The “ch” in machine is /ʃ/, as in shoe. Church and chair have /tʃ/; character has /k/.

questions.subject: use-of-english
questions.stem: In which word is the “b” silent?
questions.explanation: In climb, the final b is not pronounced: /klaɪm/. In the others, the b is heard.

questions.subject: use-of-english
questions.stem: Which word rhymes with “weight”?
questions.explanation: Weight is pronounced /weɪt/, which rhymes with late /leɪt/. Height has /aɪ/, despite the similar spelling.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.context: Kemi had saved for months to buy a second-hand sewing machine. In the first week she made only two dresses, and one of them had a crooked hem. Her neighbour laughed and told her to go back to selling oranges. Kemi said nothing. She unpicked the hem, sewed it again, and hung the dress in her window as a reminder. A year later, three girls from the street were learning the trade from her, and the neighbour had become a customer.
questions.stem: Why did Kemi hang the dress in her window?
options: As a reminder of her early mistake and how she put it right
Because it was her best work
Because no one would buy it
questions.explanation: The passage says she hung it “as a reminder”, after fixing the crooked hem: a reminder of the mistake and of not giving up.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals: The judge was IMPARTIAL in the case.
questions.explanation: Impartial means not favouring either side: fair.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in capitals: His speech was VERBOSE.
questions.explanation: Verbose means using more words than needed. The opposite is concise: short and clear.

whyNot.A: Long is close in meaning to verbose.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: Each of the boys ___ given a book.
questions.explanation: “Each” is singular, so it takes a singular verb: “Each of the boys was given a book.”

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: She is good ___ mathematics.
questions.explanation: We say “good at” a subject or skill.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: The thief was caught RED-HANDED. This means he was caught
questions.explanation: “Caught red-handed” is an idiom: caught while doing something wrong.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence.
questions.explanation: The question mark belongs to the question, inside the quotation marks; the sentence ends with a full stop after “asked”.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: I look forward to ___ from you.
questions.explanation: In “look forward to”, “to” is a preposition, so it is followed by the -ing form: hearing.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: What is the plural of “passer-by”?
questions.explanation: In a compound like passer-by, the main word (passer) takes the plural: passers-by.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: Which word contains the vowel sound /æ/, as in “cat”?
questions.explanation: Bat has /æ/. Bet has /e/, but has /ʌ/, and bait has /eɪ/.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as the one in “boat”.
questions.explanation: Boat and note have the diphthong /əʊ/. Bought has /ɔː/, bout has /aʊ/, but has /ʌ/.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: Which word is stressed on the first syllable?
questions.explanation: The noun REcord is stressed on the first syllable (the verb reCORD on the second). beGIN, aGREE and hoTEL are stressed on the second.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: Which word has the same sound as the “th” in “think”?
questions.explanation: Think and thin have the voiceless /θ/. This, then and that have the voiced /ð/.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: Which word rhymes with “cough”?
questions.explanation: Cough is /kɒf/, which rhymes with off /ɒf/. Tough is /tʌf/, through /θruː/, though /ðəʊ/: same spelling, different sounds.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: In which word is the “k” silent?
questions.explanation: In knee (and knife, know), the k before n is not pronounced: /niː/.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.context: Every morning before school, Tunde walked his younger sister to the bus stop. The road was busy and the pavement was broken in places, so he always walked on the outside, nearest the traffic, holding her hand. One day she asked him why. “Because if anything comes too close,” he said, “it should meet me first.” She did not fully understand until years later, when she found herself walking her own son along the same road, holding his hand the same way.
questions.stem: Why did Tunde walk on the side nearest the traffic?
options: Because the pavement was smooth there
To protect his sister from danger
So that his sister could see the buses
questions.explanation: He explains: if anything came too close, “it should meet me first”. He was shielding her.

questions.subject: english-language

questions.stem: “It should meet me first” shows that Tunde was
questions.explanation: He was willing to put himself between his sister and danger: protective.

One day she asked him why. “Because if anything comes too close,” he said, “it should meet me first.” She did not fully understand until years later, when she found herself walking her own son along the same road, holding his hand the same way.
questions.stem: When did his sister fully understand his reason?
options: Years later, when she walked her own son along the road
questions.explanation: “She did not fully understand until years later, when she found herself walking her own son along the same road.”

questions.subject: english-language

The road was busy and the pavement was broken in places, so he always walked on the outside, nearest the traffic, holding her hand. One day she asked him why. “Because if anything comes too close,” he said, “it should meet me first.” She did not fully understand until years later, when she found herself walking her own son along the same road, holding his hand the same way.
questions.stem: How is the road described?
options: Busy, with the pavement broken in places
questions.explanation: “The road was busy and the pavement was broken in places.”

questions.subject: english-language
questions.context: Every morning before school, Tunde walked his younger sister to the bus stop. The road was busy and the pavement was broken in places, so he always walked on the outside, nearest the traffic, holding her hand. One day she asked him why. “Because if anything comes too close,” he said, “it should meet me first.” She did not fully understand until years later, when she found herself walking her own son along the same road, holding his hand the same way.
questions.stem: In the last sentence, “the same way” refers to
options: walking on the side nearest the traffic, holding the child's hand
questions.explanation: She walks her son just as Tunde walked her: on the traffic side, holding his hand.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.context: Every morning before school, Tunde walked his younger sister to the bus stop. The road was busy and the pavement was broken in places, so he always walked on the outside, nearest the traffic, holding her hand. One day she asked him why. “Because if anything comes too close,” he said, “it should meet me first.” She did not fully understand until years later, when she found herself walking her own son along the same road, holding his hand the same way.
questions.stem: The main idea of the passage is that
options: care for others is passed on from one generation to the next
children should walk to school alone
questions.explanation: The sister does for her son what her brother did for her: the care is handed down.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals: The villagers were HOSTILE to the strangers.
questions.explanation: Hostile means unfriendly or aggressive.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in capitals: Water is SCARCE in the village this season.
questions.explanation: Scarce means in short supply. The opposite is plentiful.

whyNot.B: Rare is close in meaning to scarce.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: The news ___ good.
questions.explanation: “News” looks plural but is an uncountable noun and takes a singular verb: “The news is good.”

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: He apologised ___ coming late.
questions.explanation: We apologise to someone for something: “He apologised for coming late.”

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: TO LET THE CAT OUT OF THE BAG means
questions.explanation: “Let the cat out of the bag” is an idiom: to tell a secret, often by accident.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: Necessary has one c and a double s: ne-ces-sa-ry.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: She ___ in Abuja for five years before she moved to Lagos.
questions.explanation: The living in Abuja happened before another past action (moving to Lagos), so it takes the past perfect: had lived.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: This is the boy ___ bag was stolen.
questions.explanation: “Whose” shows possession (the boy's bag). “Who's” means “who is”.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: Which word has a different vowel sound from the others?
questions.explanation: Book, look and cook have the short /ʊ/. Boot has the long /uː/.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as the one in “bird”.
questions.explanation: Bird and word have /ɜː/. Bead has /iː/, bard /ɑː/ and bud /ʌ/.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: Which word is stressed on the second syllable?
questions.explanation: poLICE is stressed on the second syllable. MARket, TEAcher and MOther are stressed on the first.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: Which word has the same consonant sound as the “s” in “pleasure”?
questions.explanation: The “s” in pleasure and measure is /ʒ/. Pressure, sugar and sure have /ʃ/.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: Which word rhymes with “bread”?
questions.explanation: Bread /bred/ rhymes with said /sed/: different spellings, the same /e/ sound.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: In which word is the “w” silent?
questions.explanation: In write (and wrong, wrap), the w before r is not pronounced: /raɪt/.
